Annual Meetings

Afternoon Session - 2016 Meeting

Warren Buffett talks about his concerns over what he sees as the only external threat to Berkshire Hathaway's economic well-being over time. He and Charlie Munger also explain why compensation plans shouldn't reward profits, and the source of their sense of humor.

Sat, Apr 30 2016 • 1:00 PM EDT
Key Chapters —
  1. 2. Our culture will endure for "many, many decades"
  2. 6. Buffett's concerns about weapons of mass destruction
  3. 11. We've "avoided the self-destructive behavior"
  4. 12. Due diligence doesn't find the real risks of buying a company
  5. 13. "We don't pay any attention to titles"
  6. 15. 3G's cost cutting hasn't hurt Kraft Heinz
  7. 21. Don't reward profits in compensation plans
  8. 33. Where Buffett and Munger get their sense of humor
